h: Planning Your LEGOLAND Day Like a Pro
p: A big day at LEGOLAND is all about planning, and the grown-ups who've done it before tend to swear by a few golden rules. First up, arrive early. Being there for opening gives you a head start on the most popular rides before the queues build, and you'll find the whole park feels calmer in the first hour or so.

Next, think about which parts of the park suit your kids best. Toddlers and little ones tend to love DUPLO Valley, with its gentle rides and splash play areas, while older children often head for the bigger rides in areas like the Kingdom of the Pharaohs, LEGO NINJAGO World and the mythical creatures of LEGO Mythica. A quick look at the park map before you go can save a lot of walking back and forth.

Food and drink are a big part of the day. There are plenty of places to eat around the park, but many families bring a picnic and find a spot on the grass to save time and money. Take refillable water bottles, sun cream in summer and waterproofs for the rest of the year, as much of the park is outdoors.

Getting there is fairly straightforward. The park is a couple of miles from Windsor town centre, and there's a shuttle bus from Windsor when the park is open. Windsor has two stations, Windsor and Eton Central and Windsor and Eton Riverside, with trains from London. If you're driving, the M4 is close by, with plenty of parking on site.

If you're staying overnight, Windsor makes a great base. Windsor Great Park and the Long Walk are perfect for a stroll, and Eton is just over the bridge across the Thames, with its famous college and pretty high street.
